title: Choose the visual world for n1ghtly.dev
question: Safer round, steered to a smooth modern 2026 SaaS UI with fluid motion. Every card stays dark and green. Pick one, or steer again.

options.label: Bento Showcase
options.lineage: 2025-26 product sites (Apple, Vercel, Linear feature grids)
options.thesis: One screen holds every project as a tile sized by how much it matters, each showing the real thing working rather than describing it.
materials: soft-edged tiles on a deep green-black ground
options.viewport: Name and one line at top left; under it a bento: Couplet as the big tile with a real radar screenshot, dmcl as a rebuilt Discord/Minecraft chat exchange, Temperature Alarms as a small chart (sample data, labelled), MorphicVersions marked building, plus a bio tile and a links tile.
options.risk: Bento grids are the 2025-26 default; it needs real previews and uneven tile sizes or it reads as a template.

options.label: Release Notes
options.thesis: Your work reads like a product's release notes: dated entries down a timeline, each with a real screenshot and what shipped.
options.viewport: Name and one line at top; directly under, the newest entry, Couplet, with a full-width screenshot, its date and Shipped; the timeline rail runs down the left into dmcl and the rest.
options.risk: With four projects the timeline can look thin; changelog styling is common in dev tools.

options.label: Command Menu
options.thesis: The home screen is an open, searchable command menu: every project, page and link is one keystroke or click away.
options.viewport: A centred command menu already open, listing Projects, Pages and Links; moving through it swaps a large preview of the selected project beside it.
options.risk: Puts the work behind an interaction: recruiters who just scroll may not engage, and it brings back the keyboard focus you dropped.

canonCard.label: 2026 SaaS, played straight
canonCard.thesis: The Linear / Vercel / Raycast landing page, done at their level for a person: big headline, product shot, sections that animate in smoothly.
materials: a product shot in a browser frame
canonCard.viewport: Your name as the headline with one line and two buttons (Projects, Email); below, a large Couplet screenshot in a browser frame that tilts flat as you scroll; then one section per project.
canonCard.risk: Looks like a SaaS launch page for a person; well made, but closest to everything else out there.
